You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 4, which of the following statements most accurately describes the radiological findings and the corresponding diagnosis for the patient?

A) The chest X-ray shows a centrally located mass in the left hilum with spiculated edges, suggestive of primary lung cancer.
B) The chest X-ray reveals a lobulated mass in the left hilum affecting both the upper and lower lobes, consistent with bronchocentric granulomatosis.
C) The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy without a discrete mass, typical of sarcoidosis.
D) The chest X-ray shows a pleural effusion in the right costophrenic angle, indicating possible parapneumonic effusion.
E) The chest X-ray displays diffuse interstitial infiltrates, which are characteristic of interstitial lung disease.
F) The chest X-ray indicates a cavitary lesion in the left upper lobe, suggestive of a fungal infection.
